questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important that the courses available at the destination was something that I found interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The university was very helpful and sended all the practical information was sent to my email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was shown my accomodation by the porter and all practical information was sent to my email by the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different types of rooms was available for me to choose. I could choose if I wanted an ensuite room, live with a few people or more people etc.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Every flat has a shared kitchen, but it is also possible to pay for catered food if you don't want to cook yourself, plus there are several different restaurants and cafées available at campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is primarily first year students who lives at campus, so they are very young.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I can't really remember it, other than it was quite easy because the university is very helpful at every step of the way as I recall.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always ask for help by email, and they would answer promptly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think I have any advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is alot less lecture- and seminar hours than at UCPH (depending on what you study ofc.) but I only had 8 hours a week, so there is alot of self study time, which I was not prepared for, and therefore academically I felt like I needed something more.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level on the courses was quite similar to the level I'm used to at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty similar to the one I'm used to at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
LING 221
LING 228
LING 316
LING 325

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend LING221 because it is very interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I encountered any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transportation was more expensive than I expected while the food was less expensice than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are alot of different societies at campus. You can play every kind of sport, and examples of some societies are the baking society, the Taylor Swift society, the Harry Potter society etc. It is the perfect way to meet other students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining the film society, because you get to see a movie in a big lecture hall with other people, and afterwards you can discuss the movie (if you want) with other people, but mostly just socialize in very chill settings with other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to 'the lake district' it is an absolutely beautiful area, which is very known among everybody in England, and it is very easy and fast to go there by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not that difficult since the culture in my opinion is not that different to the Danish one.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join as many societies as possible!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't think of any atm.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everybody is so kind, talkative and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy the time, it goes by very fast.
2. Travel in your weekend and in your breaks, there are so many beautiful places in the UK and they are very easily accesible by train.
3. Join societies! This way you'll get the prime university experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't think of anything else than what I have already mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding was to live with other students all from the UK, and that way really get to experience the british culture first hand.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was the feeling of missing out at events and other things at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
